subject.title: memory-lancedb auto-recall ignores per-agent memorySearch.enabled, causing cross-agent memory leakage

question: What safe default and migration contract should memory-lancedb use to prevent cross-agent memory disclosure?
rationale: The disclosure is confirmed, but the immediate configuration gate and full persisted-record partitioning provide different guarantees; prior unmerged implementations also exposed compatibility and legacy-data tradeoffs that require owner intent.

options.title: Secure by default
options.body: Honor effective memorySearch disablement and partition new records by agent, with a verified migration or explicit disposition for existing shared rows.

options.title: Land the gate first
options.body: Immediately prevent auto-recall for disabled agents, then handle broader persisted-record isolation in a separately reviewed migration.

options.title: Keep opt-in scoping
options.body: Preserve shared storage by default but add a documented LanceDB-specific scoping policy and prominent disclosure warning.

recommendation.title: Secure by default
recommendation.body: Honor effective memorySearch disablement and partition new records by agent, with a verified migration or explicit disposition for existing shared rows.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available history signal across the current plugin, effective memory configuration, and compatibility-sensitive surfaces.
